stories.title: EU, China among trading partners hit by new Trump tariffs
stories.summary: The Trump administration has imposed new tariffs of 10% and 12.5% on goods from 60 trading partners, including the EU and China, over allegations of lax enforcement of forced labour bans, just as a temporary 10% global tariff expired. The move is the White House's latest effort to restore President Donald ⁠Trump's campaign vision of a near-global tariff after the US Supreme Court in February struck down his "reciprocal" duties of 10% to 50% imposed last year under a national emergencies law to try to shrink the US trade deficit. The new tariffs, announced late last night in a Federal Register notice, cover 99.4% of US imports, but include numerous product exemptions, such as oil and gas, fertiliser and certain food items. Imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, the new duties allow the administration to maintain a tariff floor on virtually all US imports despite the Supreme Court setback.

stories.title: 'No adverse' Aughinish findings, but lack of Russian data
stories.summary: An independent review into Aughinish Alumina exports to Russia has made no "adverse findings" against the plant, but the Minister for Enterprise cited a "lack of verifiable internal trade data within Russia" since the country's invasion of Ukraine. The review follows reports of alleged exports of alumina to Russian weapons manufacturers from the Co Limerick facility. It comes as the Taoiseach Micheál Martin yesterday said the Government's investigation into Aughinish Alumina has not found definitive proof linking its alumina exports to weapons manufacturers in Russia. He added it neither found "definitive evidence that alumina may not be going to weapons manufacturers".

stories.title: Fresh strikes as US vows retaliation for Houthi attacks
stories.summary: The United States has launched a fresh wave of strikes on Iranian military targets, marking the 13th successive night of active combat in the region. The latest volley comes the night after Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen opened a new front in the war with attacks on oil tankers in Red Sea shipping lanes - though US Central Command (CENTCOM) did not specifically mention the rebel blockade in announcing the latest offensive. Iranian state media reported that US missiles hit the southwestern city of Ahvaz, and explosions were heard in nearby Omidiyeh, as well as the port city of Bandar Abbas and the island of Qeshm on the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM said the attacks "aimed to hold Iran accountable and diminish threats from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to commercial shipping".

stories.title: MetroLink, Galway ring road among fast-tracked projects
stories.summary: The Government will today announce a list of nine projects to be fast-tracked under new legislation that prioritises critical infrastructure. Among the schemes that will be listed are Dublin's MetroLink, the Cork Area Commuter Rail Programme and the Galway ring road. The new legislation, proposed by Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers, was enacted last month. It mandates public bodies involved in authorising projects to fast-track specific schemes, which have been designated as critical by the Government.

stories.title: Emergency declared in Madrid as wildfires sweep Europe
stories.summary: Wildfires fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds swept through parts of Italy, France and Spain, forcing thousands of people to flee as hundreds of firefighters backed by water-bombing planes battled the blazes. Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures severe heat, with temperatures topping 40C in some areas. Spain has declared a national emergency in the Madrid region and in the province of Avila, near the capital, in the wake of several wildfires burning out of control. The measure, announced by the interior ministry late last night, aims to speed up the deployment of resources to fight the fires, and places the response to the crisis in the hands of a military emergency unit.

stories.title: Kerry fans confident of 40th All-Ireland football title
stories.summary: Kerry will bid for an unprecedented 40th All-Ireland football title when they take on Mayo in Croke Park on Sunday. No other county has been as successful as Kerry in football - Dublin are second on the roll of honour with 31 victories. Title number 40 is now within sight for the Kingdom, with just one more match and Mayo standing in the way. Its mostly down to hard work and the honing of skills from an early age in nurseries, schools and clubs throughout the county, like at Beaufort GAA club in mid-Kerry, a beautiful plain at the foot of the MacGillycuddy Reeks.

stories.title: Park rangers to be able to issue fines under by-law plans
stories.summary: The Government has announced it is drafting a new National Parks Bill that would allow for by-laws prohibiting or restricting certain activities, like the use of disposable barbecues, alongside other sanctions, in the country's national parks. Until now, national parks have been managed through a range of legislative and administrative arrangements. However, there is no comprehensive statutory framework dedicated specifically to their designation, governance and management. The move will align Ireland with international best practice and enable the State to provide "a coherent and enduring basis for their protection, restoration and management".

stories.title: Minister signals BAM should not bid for hospital project
stories.summary: The Minister for Health has indicated that contractor BAM should not tender for the new National Maternity Hospital project at Elm Park, as she revealed that she has informed Cabinet about fire certification problems at the National Children's Hospital, for which BAM is responsible. Jennifer Carroll MacNeill said that the business case for the new maternity facility on the St Vincent's Hospital grounds will be brought to Cabinet this autumn. She noted that a lot of the preparatory work has been ongoing at the site, and said that the tendering process will not get underway until the Cabinet approves the project. When asked about further reported delays to the National Children’s Hospital, the minister said that she brought a memo to Cabinet this week which has detailed issues which have arisen.
